review_basis: Third byte-bound review of the eight replacement clips generated after the second review. Every decision is tied to the replacement media SHA-256, its twelve-frame contact-sheet SHA-256 and the narrowed claim/slice role in footage_use_contracts.json.

decisions.reason: The contact sheet shows shipyard welding beside a large hull, not a scientific or offshore working vessel carrying the narrated expedition and surface-logistics context.
The frames show only the dark ocean surface and never reveal a seabed, abyssal plane, benthic survey, submersible or underwater exploration context.
Container cranes at a commercial dock do not show marine pipe handling, offshore machinery or the physical operation required by the technical-test assignments.
A textile-factory worker operating machinery is not a control-room operator monitoring a marine or industrial technical system and cannot carry the shared-ocean decision premise.
A brightly lit recreational shipwreck cannot represent measured long-term disturbance, persistent mining tracks or a restrained scientific benthic-survey context.
The fishing boat lacks scientific personnel, survey instruments or visible offshore technical equipment and would falsely imply that ordinary fishing activity represents the expedition.
The reviewed frames clearly show a populated formal assembly with presenters and an engaged audience, providing valid generic human governance context without identifying a named institution.
The clear-water shipwreck, reef and fish imagery is recreational underwater beauty footage, not a dark abyssal descent or persistent deep-seabed context.
